title: Perplexity Filter Evasion Rate as a Function of Attack Sophistication

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: perplexity filters are widely deployed but their coverage across attack sophistication levels is poorly understood. The evasion rate map directly shows which attack classes they fail on, motivating layered defenses.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Computing perplexity with GPT-2 and classifying attacks by category uses standard tools. The comparison against activation probes adds some complexity, but the core experiment is scripting-level. Guided beginners can execute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: TPR/FPR table per attack category for a perplexity filter. Uses existing benchmark data. Can drop the activation probe comparison to tighten scope further. Fits in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Perplexity-based jailbreak detection and its evasion are well-studied. 'Detecting Language Model Attacks With Perplexity' (OpenReview) establishes the baseline defense. 'A Hybrid Perplexity-MAS Framework' (2025) extends it with multi-agent systems. 'Bypassing LLM Guardrails' (arXiv:2504.11168) empirically demonstrates evasion of guardrails including perplexity filters. PAPILLON and AutoDAN specifically optimize low-perplexity adversarial prompts. The systematic mapping of evasion rates by attack category/sophistication level is a useful framing but the individual findings (that sophisticated attacks evade perplexity filters) are already known from multiple papers.
